source.title: Polar Broad Absorption Line Quasars: An Open Question

accepted.question_text: What fraction of broad absorption line (BAL) quasars are genuinely "polar", in the sense that they contain relativistic jets oriented close to our line of sight, and how does the incidence of such line-of-sight jets in BAL quasars compare with that in non-BAL quasars when the classification is based on very long baseline interferometry (VLBI) measurements of brightness temperature, repeated imaging, and apparent transverse jet motions rather than on two-epoch radio flux-density variability alone?

evidence.quote: Only VLBI imaging can robustly determine the fraction of broad absorption line quasars which are polar.
determining the relative incidence of relativistic jets oriented along our line of sight in normal and BAL quasars will require VLBI imaging to directly measure brightness temperatures.
